title: Excel Saga
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Excel and Hyatt work minimum-wage jobs to support their real mission: conquering the city of Fukuoka for ACROSS, a secret organization run by the aloof Il Palazzo, which consists of little more than a basement, the two interns and a stray dog. The long-running absurdist parody resets its failed missions over and over while satirizing city government, religion and public television, and grows a larger plot about cosmic forces over 27 volumes.
life_message: Life is absurd and grand causes use up ordinary people, so laugh and keep going.

content.note: Constant slapstick violence: Hyatt repeatedly dies, Excel dropped into a pit, neighbors assault each other (Gaffney review; MU Action).
Fan service grows in later volumes (Gaffney); MU Ecchi and Big Breasts; MangaDex suggestive. MU Pedophilia category unexplained (to verify).
Characters losing memory and identity (AniList review); Hyatt's illness as gag.
Cartoon cruelty to a dog played for laughs (Viz blurb).
Parodies public television and pop culture.

dominant: Absurdist parody; satire of institutions; cynical view of grand causes

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Slights answered with comic violence among neighbors (Gaffney).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Organizational loyalty (ACROSS, city hall) over family.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Excel's devotion to Il Palazzo is the running joke of hierarchy.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Characters scrape by on part-time jobs yet chase personal causes.

folkways.japan: Local Fukuoka setting, part-time work and sentai/tokusatsu parody draw on Japanese pop culture and city life.

delivery.evidence: AniList review calls the tone cynical and arbitrary but 'not quite nihilistic'; Gaffney calls it 'just plain fun' with no moral.
delivery.note: Everything, including its own villains and institutions, is a target of parody rather than a vehicle for one message.

winners_losers: No side clearly wins; ACROSS and the city both look foolish, and the reviewer sees ordinary people used up by cosmic forces.
